record.paper_title: Discrepancy estimates for sequences: new results and open problems
record.original_question: Improve Kritzer's discrepancy bound for hybrid point sets obtained by combining a Hammersley point set with a good lattice point set, gaining almost a logarithmic factor over the bound stated in Theorem 3.2.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9 Improve the result of Kritzer cited in Theorem 3.2 above on the discrepancy of Hammersley-good lattice point-sets by almost a logarithmic factor.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $s_1, s_2 \geq 1$ be integers and set $s = s_1 + s_2$. For an integer $m \geq 1$, let $N = 2^m$. The two-dimensional Hammersley point set in base $2$ with $N$ points is
$$\mathcal{H}_N = \left\{\left(\tfrac{n}{N},\, \phi_2(n)\right) : n = 0, 1, \ldots, N-1\right\} \subset [0,1)^2,$$
where $\phi_2$ is the base-$2$ radical-inverse function. More generally, an $s_1$-dimensional Hammersley-type point set $\mathcal{H}_N^{(s_1)} \subset [0,1)^{s_1}$ is constructed analogously using $s_1 - 1$ pairwise coprime bases together with the coordinate $n/N$.

For a generating vector $\mathbf{g} = (g_1, \ldots, g_{s_2}) \in \mathbb{Z}^{s_2}$ with $\gcd(g_i, N) = 1$, the associated good lattice point set in dimension $s_2$ is
$$\mathcal{L}_N(\mathbf{g}) = \left\{\left(\left\{\tfrac{n g_1}{N}\right\}, \ldots, \left\{\tfrac{n g_{s_2}}{N}\right\}\right) : n = 0, 1, \ldots, N-1\right\} \subset [0,1)^{s_2}.$$

The hybrid (Hammersley–good lattice) point set is
$$\mathcal{P}_N = \left\{(\mathbf{x}_n, \mathbf{y}_n) : n = 0, 1, \ldots, N-1\right\} \subset [0,1)^s,$$
where $\mathbf{x}_n$ is the $n$-th point of $\mathcal{H}_N^{(s_1)}$ and $\mathbf{y}_n$ is the $n$-th point of $\mathcal{L}_N(\mathbf{g})$.

The star discrepancy of a finite point set $\mathcal{P} \subset [0,1)^s$ is
$$D_N^*(\mathcal{P}) = \sup_{\mathbf{t} \in [0,1]^s} \left| \frac{\#\{n : \mathbf{p}_n \in [\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{t})\}}{N} - \prod_{i=1}^s t_i \right|.$$

It is known that there exists a generating vector $\mathbf{g}$ such that
$$N\, D_N^*(\mathcal{P}_N) = O\!\left((\log N)^{s}\right),$$
with an implied constant depending only on $s$.

Problem. Show that there exists a choice of generating vector $\mathbf{g}$ for which the bound can be improved to
$$N\, D_N^*(\mathcal{P}_N) = O\!\left((\log N)^{s-1+\varepsilon}\right) \quad \text{or} \quad O\!\left((\log N)^{s-1} (\log\log N)^{c}\right)$$
for some constant $c > 0$, thereby gaining almost a full factor of $\log N$ over the previously known bound.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaces follow-up work on hybrid point sets combining Hammersley/Halton-type and (polynomial) lattice point sets, including component-by-component constructions and existence results, but none of the located references explicitly claim to improve the relevant Kritzer star-discrepancy bound by almost a logarithmic factor. The status of this specific improvement could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: On hybrid point sets stemming from Halton-type Hammersley point sets and polynomial lattice point sets
status_evidence.snippet: Existence results for finite hybrid point sets with low discrepancy combining Halton-type Hammersley sets with polynomial lattice point sets.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work studies hybrid Hammersley/lattice point sets but does not explicitly improve the Kritzer bound by almost a log factor.

status_evidence.title: Component-by-Component Construction of Hybrid Point Sets Based on Hammersley and Lattice Point Sets
status_evidence.snippet: CBC construction of hybrid point sets based on Hammersley and lattice point sets.
status_evidence.claim: Provides explicit constructions but the discrepancy bound order matches earlier existence results.
